Explain Enabled everywhere/Disabled everywhere versus Let organizations decide, explicit feature preservation, previews excluded, and a distinct model default/explicit override. Qualify generic 'a default can allow lower-level overrides': review-effort default can be overridden, but feature/model policy states may prevent it.
findings.original_learning_change: Expand Lab7 tabletop: enterprise Enabled everywhere initially materializes feature F; later changing global default to Disabled does not rewrite F's now-set policy under the Oct22 migration rule. Explicitly disabling F is a separate action. A review-effort setting overridden at repository scope does not change feature authorization. Include delegated organization and preview rows. Preserve release note versus live settings evidence.

findings.remaining_gap: Current evergreen wording focuses on future unconfigured defaults; dated release specifically describes one-time migration. Retain both contracts and actual-state inspection; no tenant completion claim.

findings.observation: Current how-to explicitly says Copilot CLI and IDE Agent mode do not support content exclusion; Sept2 GA announcement explicitly says CLI/app respect it for Business/Enterprise.
findings.proposed_repair: Replace categorical CLI-support statements with dated conflict note citing both pages. Keep IDE Agent-mode limitation and no-secret-management guarantee. State announcement-supported intended CLI behavior is not consistently documented in current how-to, and client/plan/policy behavior needs a disposable test.
findings.original_learning_change: Add Lab4 evidence matrix with plan, client/version, exclusion pattern, license source, feature path and observed context. Use unique nonsensitive marker in excluded file and allowed control file; test supported inline/Chat, IDE Agent and CLI separately. An absent marker in prose alone does not prove file was never read; inspect tool activity/configuration. Report not-run separately.
findings.objective_fit: Privacy, exclusions and safeguards; tests reasoning across surfaces.

findings.confidence: Confirmed product documentation; no client validation
findings.observation: Current cloud MCP calls run autonomously without approval. Registry enforcement is weaker than managed-settings allowlisting; allowlists can match URL or command and deny rules prevail. Surface support is not universal; cloud/code-review accept tools only and remote OAuth unsupported. readOnlyHint limits eligibility, not proof a tool implementation cannot mutate.
findings.proposed_repair: Add surface-specific paragraph and a compact trust table separating client policy, server allowlist, tool selection, credential scope and downstream authorization. Prefer managed settings for applicable clients while checking each property's client support. Do not imply local interactive approval applies to cloud agent.
findings.original_learning_change: In Lab5, compare same nominal server name at approved and altered URL/stdio command. Paper-design rejection by actual matching rule, then inventory a read-only and write-capable tool plus effective credential. Cloud task requiring pre-write approval must enforce approval in service/workflow or omit write tool; a prompt alone is insufficient.
findings.objective_fit: Responsible use, agents/context/data and safeguards. Managed-settings details are related implementation depth.
findings.remaining_gap: No enterprise settings changed. MCP concept page says policy disabled by default while default-availability policy can enable eligible unconfigured settings: inspect effective state rather than repeat universal default.

findings.original_learning_change: Lab3 tabletop first: classify permission mode, enterprise permitted modes, tool/path/URL rules, requested action, automatic versus human decision and actual execution record. findings.confidence: Confirmed capability boundaries; local brand/symbol policy design original, not vendor classifier guarantee
findings.observation: Guide's generic visual safety is too thin for policy enforcement and marks. Image harm classification covers specified harm categories; a harmless-looking logo/watermark can still violate application brand policy. Provenance provides origin/history signals, not content permission, truth, authorship or endorsement.
findings.proposed_repair: Add separate policy pipeline: inspect image+embedded text, collect evidence/candidates, compare to approved local brand/symbol rules, route uncertain cases to reviewer, enforce allow/block/review in application before publishing. Define official logos/brand assets as governed references; do not equate a model's visual guess with rights clearance. Distinguish visible watermark/brand matching from invisible provenance and signed C2PA metadata. Supported models/features are VERIFY CURRENT; transforms can remove signals.
findings.original_learning_change: Four synthetic assets: permitted fictional logo with signed provenance; disallowed fictional mark with otherwise safe content; ambiguous cropped symbol; image with untrusted embedded instruction. Worksheet fields: mediaID, observed region/text, candidate label+uncertainty, approved policy rule/version, harm class, provenance signal/verification, decision+reviewer, publication enforcement/evidence. Expected: safe harm score does not override disallowed mark; uncertain symbol goes review; C2PA does not grant publishing rights; embedded instruction never authorizes action. Use original geometric fictional marks, no offensive imagery.
